name: Question 11
worked_solution:
Here, the first factor is $4\times 1$ matrix and the second factor is a $1\times 3$ matrix. 

There is $1$ column in the first matrix and $1$ row in the second matrix, so the product is well defined:

$$
4\times \boxed{\text{1}}✓\boxed{\text{1}}\times 3=4\times 3
$$

Computing the product, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 6 \\ 0 \\ 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-10\cdot 1 & -10\cdot (-5) & -10\cdot (-1) \\ 6\cdot 1 & 6\cdot (-5) & 6\cdot (-1) \\ 0\cdot 1 & 0\cdot (-5) & 0\cdot (-1) \\ 8\cdot 1 & 8\cdot (-5) & 8\cdot (-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10 & 50 & 10 \\ 6 & -30 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & -40 & -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
